LH-PROV-004.explanation: North Carolina requires a 31-day grace period on individual life policies (G.S. 58-58-22(1)), so the policy was still in force when the insured died on March 20. The insurer pays the face amount minus the overdue premium: $100,000 - $1,200 = $98,800, not the full $100,000.

LH-HPRV-001.explanation: North Carolina's grace period provision (G.S. 58-51-15) sets at least 10 days for monthly premiums, so coverage continues through June 11 and any unpaid premium can be deducted from a claim. The 7-day minimum applies only to weekly premiums, and 31 days to other modes.

LH-GEN-015.explanation: G.S. 58-3-10 makes every statement in a North Carolina application a representation, not a warranty, and a representation that is neither material nor fraudulent does not prevent recovery. A warranty would have to be literally true, which the law does not require.
